literal: The whole state grieved and wept for him; Emperor Daowu several times pursued remembrance in wounded grief.
idiomatic: The whole state grieved and wept for him; Emperor Daowu several times pursued remembrance in wounded grief.

literal: Posthumously Prince of Chenliu Huan, enshrined in the ancestral temple; his son Yue was enfeoffed Prince of Zhuti.
idiomatic: Posthumously Prince of Chenliu Huan, enshrined in the ancestral temple; his son Yue was enfeoffed Prince of Zhuti.

literal: Yue was outwardly harmonious yet inwardly fierce.
idiomatic: Yue was outwardly harmonious yet inwardly fierce.

literal: Emperor Daowu because Prince Huan died for the royal house specially added intimate favor; he was made Left General and inherited the enfeoffment, later Clan Mentor.
idiomatic: Emperor Daowu because Prince Huan died for the royal house specially added intimate favor; he was made Left General and inherited the enfeoffment, later Clan Mentor.

literal: Yue relied on favor and was arrogant; he often said to intimates Wang Luosheng and the like, "Once the imperial carriage passes in peace, I shall only avoid the Duke of Wei.
idiomatic: Yue relied on favor and was arrogant; he often said to intimates Wang Luosheng and the like, "Once the imperial carriage passes in peace, I shall only avoid the Duke of Wei.

literal: Apart from this, who shall be before me!"
idiomatic: Apart from this, who shall be before me!"

literal: Prince of Wei Yi had a beautiful beard and was weighty within and without—therefore Yue spoke thus.
idiomatic: Prince of Wei Yi had a beautiful beard and was weighty within and without—therefore Yue spoke thus.

literal: At first when Yao Xing ransomed Di Bozhi, Yue sent him on the way; the route passed Yanmen.
idiomatic: At first when Yao Xing ransomed Di Bozhi, Yue sent him on the way; the route passed Yanmen.

literal: Yue thereby in secret enticed treacherous magnates to win their hearts.
idiomatic: Yue thereby in secret enticed treacherous magnates to win their hearts.

literal: Later when matters were found out he fled in fear, threw himself on Yanmen, plotted to gather heroes and act unlawfully, and was by the natives seized and sent.
idiomatic: Later when matters were found out he fled in fear, threw himself on Yanmen, plotted to gather heroes and act unlawfully, and was by the natives seized and sent.

literal: The emperor pardoned and did not punish.
idiomatic: The emperor pardoned and did not punish.

literal: When Emperor Mingyuan took the throne he led Yue in to attend; he still harbored treacherous designs and said to the emperor, "The capital's mixed people cannot be trusted and relied on—one should execute those not of our kind."
idiomatic: When Emperor Mingyuan took the throne he led Yue in to attend; he still harbored treacherous designs and said to the emperor, "The capital's mixed people cannot be trusted and relied on—one should execute those not of our kind."

literal: Again he said, "Yanmen's people are mostly deceitful—all may be executed."
idiomatic: Again he said, "Yanmen's people are mostly deceitful—all may be executed."

literal: He wished thereby to wash his private resentment; the emperor did not follow.
idiomatic: He wished thereby to wash his private resentment; the emperor did not follow.

literal: Yue inwardly suspected and feared; he bore a blade into attendance and plotted great treason.
idiomatic: Yue inwardly suspected and feared; he bore a blade into attendance and plotted great treason.

literal: Shusun Jun suspected him.
idiomatic: Shusun Jun suspected him.

literal: Secretly viewing his breast he had a blade; he seized him and granted death.
idiomatic: Secretly viewing his breast he had a blade; he seized him and granted death.

literal: Son Jian inherited, demoted to duke, post General Who Pacifies the North, Great General of the Wilderness-Soothing Garrison.
idiomatic: Son Jian inherited, demoted to duke, post General Who Pacifies the North, Great General of the Wilderness-Soothing Garrison.

literal: He died.
idiomatic: He died.

literal: Jian's son Chen, posts Inspector of Heng and Xi Provinces.
idiomatic: Jian's son Chen, posts Inspector of Heng and Xi Provinces.

literal: Chen's son Yi, Minister of the Secretariat Left Deputy.
idiomatic: Chen's son Yi, Minister of the Secretariat Left Deputy.

literal: Yi's son Hui.
idiomatic: Yi's son Hui.

literal: Hui styled Shuping; beard and brows like painting; bearing and deportment admirable.
idiomatic: Hui styled Shuping; beard and brows like painting; bearing and deportment admirable.

literal: He loved to range through books and records; from youth he had a fine name in the capital.
idiomatic: He loved to range through books and records; from youth he had a fine name in the capital.

literal: Zhou Wen honored him and ordered him to roam and dwell with the princes; each time shared inkstone and mat, affection exceptionally thick.
idiomatic: Zhou Wen honored him and ordered him to roam and dwell with the princes; each time shared inkstone and mat, affection exceptionally thick.

literal: Twice promoted to Martial Baron Lower Grand Master.
idiomatic: Twice promoted to Martial Baron Lower Grand Master.

literal: At the time the Turks repeatedly were border trouble; the court was about to conclude marriage alliance and ordered Hui to buy brocade one hundred thousand to send to the Turks.
idiomatic: At the time the Turks repeatedly were border trouble; the court was about to conclude marriage alliance and ordered Hui to buy brocade one hundred thousand to send to the Turks.

literal: Hui persuaded with benefit and harm; the khan was greatly pleased and sent his titled king to follow with tribute of local products.
idiomatic: Hui persuaded with benefit and harm; the khan was greatly pleased and sent his titled king to follow with tribute of local products.

literal: Soon he was made Commissioner Equal to the Three Dukes.
idiomatic: Soon he was made Commissioner Equal to the Three Dukes.

literal: When Emperor Wu of Zhou married the Turkic empress he ordered Hui to convey courtesy.
idiomatic: When Emperor Wu of Zhou married the Turkic empress he ordered Hui to convey courtesy.

literal: Granted Opening of the Office, transferred Minister of Justice.
idiomatic: Granted Opening of the Office, transferred Minister of Justice.

literal: When the east of the Pass was pacified he sent Hui to settle Hebei, enfeoffed Viscount of Yining.
idiomatic: When the east of the Pass was pacified he sent Hui to settle Hebei, enfeoffed Viscount of Yining.

literal: When Emperor Wen of Sui held all authority he added Upper Opening of the Office and advanced to duke.
idiomatic: When Emperor Wen of Sui held all authority he added Upper Opening of the Office and advanced to duke.

literal: At the beginning of Kaihuang he was made Minister of Justice, concurrently overseeing the Grand Stud.
idiomatic: At the beginning of Kaihuang he was made Minister of Justice, concurrently overseeing the Grand Stud.

literal: He received an edict to decide the Duyang water irrigation of the Sanzhi plain, irrigating several thousand qing of salty barren land—men relied on the benefit.
idiomatic: He received an edict to decide the Duyang water irrigation of the Sanzhi plain, irrigating several thousand qing of salty barren land—men relied on the benefit.

literal: Again transferred Minister of War, supervising the canal transport labor.
idiomatic: Again transferred Minister of War, supervising the canal transport labor.

literal: Before long, for an offense he was dismissed.
idiomatic: Before long, for an offense he was dismissed.

literal: Shortly after, he was made Inspector of Wei Province and had quite benevolent government.
idiomatic: Shortly after, he was made Inspector of Wei Province and had quite benevolent government.

literal: Later because of illness he left office and died in the capital.
idiomatic: Later because of illness he left office and died in the capital.

literal: The emperor sighed in grief long and ordered the Court of Imperial Entertainments to supervise the funeral, posthumous title Yuan.
idiomatic: The emperor sighed in grief long and ordered the Court of Imperial Entertainments to supervise the funeral, posthumous title Yuan.

literal: Son Su inherited, post Vice Director of the Imperial Household.
idiomatic: Son Su inherited, post Vice Director of the Imperial Household.

literal: Su's younger brother Ren, nature bright and keen, post Assistant of Rinan commandery.
idiomatic: Su's younger brother Ren, nature bright and keen, post Assistant of Rinan commandery.

literal: Jian's younger brother's legitimate son Zuo, styled Longshou.
idiomatic: Jian's younger brother's legitimate son Zuo, styled Longshou.

literal: Emperor Xuanwu reviewed martial arts; each year-end an edict ordered teaching and drill for military review.
idiomatic: Emperor Xuanwu reviewed martial arts; each year-end an edict ordered teaching and drill for military review.

literal: At first Jian because his son's offense lost the title; Zuo sought the original enfeoffment.
idiomatic: At first Jian because his son's offense lost the title; Zuo sought the original enfeoffment.

literal: The authorities memorialized permitting Zuo to inherit the duke; the princely title was not lightly given—together they sought further deliberation; an edict followed it.
idiomatic: The authorities memorialized permitting Zuo to inherit the duke; the princely title was not lightly given—together they sought further deliberation; an edict followed it.

literal: He died as Inspector of He Province.
idiomatic: He died as Inspector of He Province.

literal: Under Emperor Jiemin, posthumously Attendant-in-Ordinary and Minister of the Secretariat Deputy.
idiomatic: Under Emperor Jiemin, posthumously Attendant-in-Ordinary and Minister of the Secretariat Deputy.

literal: Qian's elder brother Yan, nature stern and weighty, few words.
idiomatic: Qian's elder brother Yan, nature stern and weighty, few words.

literal: Emperor Daowu often respected him; he elegantly had stratagems.
idiomatic: Emperor Daowu often respected him; he elegantly had stratagems.

literal: Following the pacification of Zhongshan, for merit he was enfeoffed Marquis of Pucheng.
idiomatic: Following the pacification of Zhongshan, for merit he was enfeoffed Marquis of Pucheng.

literal: Specially he received thick favor; given drums, horns, and feathered insignia—courtesy equal to a mountain lord.
idiomatic: Specially he received thick favor; given drums, horns, and feathered insignia—courtesy equal to a mountain lord.

literal: He governed with prestige and trust renowned; in office seven years—then Yuan Yigan replaced Yan as the commandery.
idiomatic: He governed with prestige and trust renowned; in office seven years—then Yuan Yigan replaced Yan as the commandery.

literal: At the time Yigan's son Wanyan had favor with Emperor Daowu; Yigan relied on his son and treated Yan lightly, not reporting his arrival; light horsemen suddenly came, pushing Yan from the couch and seizing his seat.
idiomatic: At the time Yigan's son Wanyan had favor with Emperor Daowu; Yigan relied on his son and treated Yan lightly, not reporting his arrival; light horsemen suddenly came, pushing Yan from the couch and seizing his seat.

literal: Yan did not know he was replaced and thought he was seized for crime.
idiomatic: Yan did not know he was replaced and thought he was seized for crime.

literal: When he knew it he was shamed at the insult and rudeness and said to Yigan, "My replacement when full is constant.
idiomatic: When he knew it he was shamed at the insult and rudeness and said to Yigan, "My replacement when full is constant.

literal: You without courtesy insult me—how can it be borne!"
idiomatic: You without courtesy insult me—how can it be borne!"

literal: He thereupon struck and killed him.
idiomatic: He thereupon struck and killed him.

literal: He fully reported the circumstances; Emperor Daowu admired him.
idiomatic: He fully reported the circumstances; Emperor Daowu admired him.

literal: Wanyan repeatedly sued and requested; then an edict made Yan pay ransom.
idiomatic: Wanyan repeatedly sued and requested; then an edict made Yan pay ransom.

literal: Yan then himself requested punishment; Emperor Daowu pardoned him and again remitted the ransom.
idiomatic: Yan then himself requested punishment; Emperor Daowu pardoned him and again remitted the ransom.

literal: He died of illness.
idiomatic: He died of illness.

literal: Prince of Piling Shun, son of Digàn.
idiomatic: Prince of Piling Shun, son of Digàn.

literal: By nature coarse and fierce.
idiomatic: By nature coarse and fierce.

literal: At the beginning of Dengguo he was enfeoffed Duke of Nan'an.
idiomatic: At the beginning of Dengguo he was enfeoffed Duke of Nan'an.

literal: When Emperor Daowu attacked Zhongshan he left Shun to guard the capital.
idiomatic: When Emperor Daowu attacked Zhongshan he left Shun to guard the capital.

literal: At the defeat at Baisi soldiers had stragglers return saying the great army had scattered and they did not know where the emperor was.
idiomatic: At the defeat at Baisi soldiers had stragglers return saying the great army had scattered and they did not know where the emperor was.

literal: Shun hearing it wished to establish himself; Mo Ti remonstrated and he stopped.
idiomatic: Shun hearing it wished to establish himself; Mo Ti remonstrated and he stopped.

literal: At the time Heli Juan and others gathered crowds and made turmoil at Yin commandery; Shun attacked but could not overcome them.
idiomatic: At the time Heli Juan and others gathered crowds and made turmoil at Yin commandery; Shun attacked but could not overcome them.

literal: He then followed the remaining officials from Baideng south into the old city of Fanzhi, blocking the Lei River as defense, to calm men's hearts.
idiomatic: He then followed the remaining officials from Baideng south into the old city of Fanzhi, blocking the Lei River as defense, to calm men's hearts.

literal: Emperor Daowu approved and advanced him to prince, post Commandant of the Capital District.
idiomatic: Emperor Daowu approved and advanced him to prince, post Commandant of the Capital District.

literal: Emperor Daowu loved Huang-Lao and several times summoned the princes and court ministers to expound it in person; those seated none were not reverent—only Shun alone sat sleeping, not looking yet spat.
idiomatic: Emperor Daowu loved Huang-Lao and several times summoned the princes and court ministers to expound it in person; those seated none were not reverent—only Shun alone sat sleeping, not looking yet spat.

literal: The emperor in anger deposed him.
idiomatic: The emperor in anger deposed him.

literal: The prince died at home.
idiomatic: The prince died at home.

literal: Duke of Liaoxi Yilie, son of Lizhen.
idiomatic: Duke of Liaoxi Yilie, son of Lizhen.

literal: He first perished under Murong Chui.
idiomatic: He first perished under Murong Chui.

literal: When Emperor Daowu campaigned against Zhongshan he abandoned wife and children to meet at Jingxing.
idiomatic: When Emperor Daowu campaigned against Zhongshan he abandoned wife and children to meet at Jingxing.

literal: When the central plains were pacified he had battle merit and was enfeoffed Duke of Liaoxi, made Administrator of Guangping.
idiomatic: When the central plains were pacified he had battle merit and was enfeoffed Duke of Liaoxi, made Administrator of Guangping.

literal: At the time He Ba was Acting Ye, Yilie by nature fierce and upright, himself as imperial kin ashamed to be below Ba, and secretly united a faction plotting to strike Ye.
idiomatic: At the time He Ba was Acting Ye, Yilie by nature fierce and upright, himself as imperial kin ashamed to be below Ba, and secretly united a faction plotting to strike Ye.

literal: Discovered, he was granted death.
idiomatic: Discovered, he was granted death.

literal: Son Bagan was broadly learned in past and present.
idiomatic: Son Bagan was broadly learned in past and present.

literal: Though his father had offense, Emperor Daowu because Bagan was kin entrusted him in his inner heart.
idiomatic: Though his father had offense, Emperor Daowu because Bagan was kin entrusted him in his inner heart.

literal: He had stratagems and repeatedly showed loyal diligence.
idiomatic: He had stratagems and repeatedly showed loyal diligence.

literal: When Emperor Mingyuan took the throne he was made Administrator of Bohai; officials and people rejoiced in him.
idiomatic: When Emperor Mingyuan took the throne he was made Administrator of Bohai; officials and people rejoiced in him.

literal: Enfeoffed Viscount of Wusui, transferred General of Pingyuan Garrison, won officers' and soldiers' hearts.
idiomatic: Enfeoffed Viscount of Wusui, transferred General of Pingyuan Garrison, won officers' and soldiers' hearts.

literal: He died; posthumous title Duke Ling.
idiomatic: He died; posthumous title Duke Ling.

literal: Son Shouluo inherited, advanced to Duke of Wuyi.
idiomatic: Son Shouluo inherited, advanced to Duke of Wuyi.

literal: He died.
idiomatic: He died.

literal: Son Chinu, General of Wuchuan Garrison.
idiomatic: Son Chinu, General of Wuchuan Garrison.

literal: Chinu's son Hongchao had quite learning; after the Mahayana rebels' turmoil an edict made Hongchao hold staff and concurrently Yellow Gate Attendant to soothe Ji province.
idiomatic: Chinu's son Hongchao had quite learning; after the Mahayana rebels' turmoil an edict made Hongchao hold staff and concurrently Yellow Gate Attendant to soothe Ji province.

literal: On return he memorialized that Ji's land was broad, the border seven or eight hundred li from the province, facing the sea dangerous and far—one should separately establish a province to guard the coastal bend.
idiomatic: On return he memorialized that Ji's land was broad, the border seven or eight hundred li from the province, facing the sea dangerous and far—one should separately establish a province to guard the coastal bend.

literal: Court deliberation followed it; later Cang Province was established.
idiomatic: Court deliberation followed it; later Cang Province was established.

literal: He died as General of the Northern Army and Grand Master of the Glorious Light.
idiomatic: He died as General of the Northern Army and Grand Master of the Glorious Light.

literal: Yilie's younger brother Bo was skilled at archery and driving; for merit he was enfeoffed Duke of Pengcheng.
idiomatic: Yilie's younger brother Bo was skilled at archery and driving; for merit he was enfeoffed Duke of Pengcheng.

literal: He died; posthumous title Que.
idiomatic: He died; posthumous title Que.

literal: Buried with honor at Jinling.
idiomatic: Buried with honor at Jinling.

literal: Eldest son Su inherited.
idiomatic: Eldest son Su inherited.

literal: Under Emperor Taiwu he supervised armies garrisoned south of the desert.
idiomatic: Under Emperor Taiwu he supervised armies garrisoned south of the desert.

literal: The Rouran reported it.
idiomatic: The Rouran reported it.

literal: Su was upright and bright, good at commanding crowds; he comforted officers and soldiers and must share their toil and rest.
idiomatic: Su was upright and bright, good at commanding crowds; he comforted officers and soldiers and must share their toil and rest.
